# dsh-windows-monitor
English | 简体中文
A system monitor overlay for DeepSeek Harness: a compact pill in the bottom-right corner showing liv
e CPU and memory, expanding into a detail card with disk activity and throughput, per-volume capacit
y, network state, uptime and battery.
Runs on **Windows**.
## Features
- **Never covers the middle.** Collapsed it is a ~210 px pill; expanded it is a 280 px card. It sits

clear of the composer by default.
- **Draggable, with no automatic snapping.** Drag the pill or the
card header freely; the panel fades slightly while moving. It stays exactly where you release it —

proximity to an edge changes nothing.
- **Explicit custom positions.** Open the card and choose **自定
义位置** to pick one of eight anchors from a 3×3 grid: four corners and four edge midpoints, with a 14
px gap (10 px on narrow screens). A docked panel stores its anchor and gap, so a resize recomputes i

ts position from that anchor and keeps it on the same edge through expand/collapse.
- **Stays out of
the window controls.** Top anchors and the drag range start below the window-chrome strip published
as `--dsh-frame-top-clearance` / `--dsh-frame-overlay-top`, so the panel never covers the titlebar
or the minimize, maximize and close buttons. Native fullscreen uses the collapsed inset automaticall

y.
- **Remembers the last placement.** A free drag coordinate or a chosen dock anchor is written to
`localStorage` and restored on the next launch, then clamped into the current safe area if the windo

w is smaller.
- **Live at a glance.** The status dot is colour-coded — green nominal, amber elevated

, pulsing red for collection failure.
- **Detail on demand.** CPU, memory and **disk activity** as b

ars, plus one row per volume, a memory total, adapter state, uptime and battery.
- **Capacity and ac
tivity are never conflated.** The 磁盘 gauge is *busy time* — the same figure as Task Manager's own 磁盘
column, computed as `100 − PercentIdleTime`. Fullness is a separate per-volume row. A static "93% f
ull" number sitting next to a live CPU reading reads as a stuck or broken dial, so it is never what

the gauge shows.
- **Unknown is a real state.** Disk activity is best-effort: with no performance-co
unter provider, or before the first sample, the panel renders `--` rather than `0%`. A zero would be

a claim about an idle disk that nothing actually measured.
[该节后续省略]
## Requirements

- DeepSeek Harness with the **Web** profile and the current profile-bundle system.
- **Windows.** Th

e host process must be running on Windows; see Platform support.
- Node.js `^22.19.0 || >=24.0.0` (t
o build from source).
No administrator rights are needed, and nothing is installed system-wide.
## Platform support
Windows only, and that is deliberate. The plugin is named for Windows, its headline reading (disk ac
tivity) comes from a Windows performance counter, and a collector the maintainer cannot run is a col
lector whose bugs they cannot reproduce. Shipping Linux and macOS collectors that were written from
documentation — and that the author could never exercise on their own hardware — traded a promise th
e project could not keep for two code paths it could not maintain.
[该节后续省略]
## How it works
The **Host half** registers one read-only route and runs the collector for its own platform through
the harness `shell` service:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The collector prints one `key=value` fact per line. A line format — rather than JSON — is deliberate
: emitting correct JSON from PowerShell without assuming a JSON library is a portability trap, where
as `key=value` is trivial to produce and trivial to parse (and unit-test) on the TypeScript side. Th
e host converts facts into the snapshot the client renders and stamps the timestamp itself.
The shell seam is driven through **both** of its entry points. DSH renamed `ctx.shell.run(spec)` to
`ctx.shell.execute(spec)`, which resolves with a handle whose `result()` carries the outcome, so the
host prefers `execute` and falls back to `run`. Hard-coding either one breaks the plugin on the har
ness versions that expose the other — `0.2.3` did exactly that and answered every poll with `ctx.she
ll.run is not a function`. `tests/collectors.test.ts` now covers both, plus a seam with neither.
Results are cached for 5 seconds, and concurrent polls share a single in-flight collection instead o
f racing, so the browser's polling never multiplies collector runs.
The **Client half** registers into the frame-wide `shell.overlay` slot. That layer is click-through
by design — the panel opts into pointer events, so it never blocks the app underneath.
Neither half touches the model, the session, or the transcript. The plugin registers no tools.
## Security model
Read this before installing.
- **The collector is read-only.** It reads CIM/WMI and runs `Get-NetAdapter`. Nothing writes, instal

ls, or changes machine state.
- **The sandbox grant is broad.** The Host half resolves the `danger-f
ull-access` sandbox policy so the shell can run. The commands are read-only, but the policy is not —

it is the main thing to review, and it lives in `src/index.ts` and `src/collectors/`.
- **The comma
nd is chosen by the host, not the browser.** The platform comes from `process.platform`; a request c

annot select a different collector.
- **The payload carries no personal data.** It contains the host
name, CPU percentage, memory totals and usage, per-volume capacity and usage, disk busy time and re
ad/write throughput, a connected-adapter count, uptime hours, and battery percentage when a battery
exists. No file contents, no usernames, no paths, no credentials, and no per-process or per-file dis

k attribution.
- **No network egress.** The plugin makes no outbound requests. Its only HTTP surface

is the local route served by the harness on your machine.
- **No secret material.** The plugin neve

r reads credentials.
- **Cache-Control: no-store** on every response.
- **One localStorage key**, ho
lding only the panel position and dock anchor (including its edge gap), never metric data.
